title: ASIC DFT Engineer
jobDescription:
Job Summary

Meet the Team:

The Common Hardware Group (CHG) delivers the silicon, optics, and hardware platforms for Cisco's core Switching, Routing, and Wireless products. We design the networking hardware for Enterprises and Service Providers of various sizes, the Public Sector, and Non-Profit Organizations across the world. Cisco Silicon One (#CiscoSiliconOne) is the only unifying silicon architecture in the market that enables customers to deploy the best-of-breed silicon from Top of Rack (TOR) switches all the way through web scale data centers and across service provider, enterprise networks, and data centers with a fully unified routing and switching portfolio.

Your Impact:

Responsible for implementing the Hardware Design-for-Test (DFT) features that support ATE, in-system test, debug and diagnostics needs of the designs.

Responsible for development of innovative DFT IP in collaboration with the multi-functional teams, and play a key role in full chip design integration with the testability features coordinated in the RTL.

Work closely with the design/design-verification and PD teams to enable the integration and validation of the Test logic in all phases of the implementation and post silicon validation flows.

Your team will participate in the creation of Innovative Hardware DFT physical design aspects for new silicon device models, bare die stacked die, driving re-usable test and debug strategies.

The job requires the candidate to have the ability to craft solutions and debug with minimal mentorship.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelors or a Master s Degree in Electrical or Computer Engineering required with at least 4-8 years of experience.
  • Knowledge of the latest innovative trends in DFT, test and silicon engineering.
  • Experience with JTAG protocols, Scan and BIST architectures, including memory BIST and boundary scan.
  • Experience with ATPG and EDA tools like TestMax, Tetramax, Tessent tool sets, PrimeTime
  • Verification skills include, System Verilog Logic Equivalency checking and validating the Test-timing of the design
  • Experience working with Gate level simulation, debugging with VCS and other simulators.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Post-silicon validation and debug experience; Ability to work with ATE patterns, P1687
  • Strong verbal skills and ability to thrive in a multifaceted environment
  • Scripting skills: Tcl, Python/Perl.

title: Social Media, Performance Ads & AI Content Intern
jobDescription:
Role Description

We are looking for a creative, energetic, and highly skilled individual who is passionate about creating engaging digital-first video content.

The ideal candidate should have a strong understanding of video editing, social media content, performance advertising, motion graphics, and AI-powered content creation.

You will work closely with our Brand, Content, Design, and Marketing teams to create high-impact videos for Instagram, Facebook, YouTube, Performance Marketing campaigns, Product Launches, and other digital platforms.

We are looking for someone who doesn't just know how to edit videos, but understands what makes people stop scrolling, watch, engage, and take action.



Job Description / Responsibilities


1. Video Editing & Content Creation


  • Edit engaging Reels, Shorts, social media videos,performance ads, product videos, and brand content.
  • Convert raw footage, product assets, images, and existing content into polished video creatives.
  • Create multiple versions and variations of videos for different campaigns and platforms.
  • Understand pacing, hooks, transitions, music, storytelling, and retention while editing.
  • Repurpose long-form content into engaging short-form videos.
  • Stay updated with trending editing styles, viral formats, transitions, and social media trends.

2. Performance Marketing Creatives


  • Create video advertisements designed specifically for Meta, YouTube, and other digital advertising platforms.
  • Understand the importance of the first 23 seconds / scroll-stopping hook in performance creatives.
  • Experiment with different hooks, opening frames,CTAs, pacing, text overlays, and video structures.
  • Create multiple creative variations for A/B testing.
  • Work with the marketing team to understand which creatives are performing and incorporate learnings into future edits.

3. Motion Graphics & Visual Effects


  • Create engaging text animations, typography, transitions, lower-thirds, call-outs, and motion graphics.
  • Have working knowledge of Adobe After Effects for creating dynamic visual elements.
  • Enhance product features and USPs using motion graphics and visual storytelling.
  • Create clean, premium, brand-consistent animations.

4. AI-Powered Video Creation


  • Experiment with AI-powered tools to enhance and speed up the video creation process.
  • Use tools such as Runway, Pika, Adobe AI tools, Kling, Higgsfield, or similar Generative AI platforms.
  • Explore AI for: Video generation, Image-to-video, Background generation/removal, AI visual effects, Voiceovers, Auto-captioning, Video enhancement, Creative experimentation.
  • Stay updated with emerging Generative AI tools and AI video trends.

5. Social Media Content


  • Understand content formats across Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, Meta Ads, YouTube, and other digital platforms.
  • Create platform-specific edits in formats such as 9:16, 1:1, 4:5, and 16:9.
  • Understand trending audio, meme formats, visual trends, and fast-paced social media editing.
  • Help the team create fresh and culturally relevant content ideas.

6. Post-Production & Quality Control


  • Perform basic to intermediate color correction and color grading.
  • Ensure proper audio levels, music synchronization, sound effects, and clean sound design.
  • Maintain smooth transitions and professional finishing across videos.
  • Export videos in the correct resolution, aspect ratio, file size, and format for different platforms.
  • Ensure all videos follow brand guidelines and visual consistency.


Must-Have Skills


Social Media Editing: Strong understanding of Reels, Shorts, trending formats, hooks, pacing, and retention-based editing.

Video Editing: Strong working knowledge of Adobe Premiere Pro or equivalent professional editing software.


After Effects: Basic to intermediate understanding of motion graphics, text animation, and visual effects


Performance Ad Editing: Basic understanding of how digital ads differ from regular social media videos.


AI Video Tools: Hands-on experimentation with Generative AI / AI-powered video or image tools.


Storytelling: Ability to turn raw footage and assets into a clear and engaging visual story.


Sound Design: Basic understanding of music selection, sound effects, audio synchronization, and audio balancing.


Creative Eye: Good sense of typography, composition, visual hierarchy, transitions, and aesthetics.


Speed & Adaptability: Ability to work on multiple creatives and adapt quickly based on feedback.


Good to have Skills:


  • Food, restaurant or FMCG content experience is an advantage.
  • Basic knowledge of Photoshop / Illustrator
  • AI image generation
  • Basic 3D / Blender / Cinema 4D knowledge
  • CGI / VFX experimentation
  • Product video editing
  • UGC-style advertisement editing
  • Meme/trend-based editing
  • Basic understanding of performance marketing metrics
  • Experience creating content for D2C, e-commerce or consumer brand

Key Software / Tools


Core: Adobe Premiere Pro | Adobe After Effects


Good to Know: Photoshop | Illustrator | DaVinci Resolve

AI / Gen AI: Runway | Pika | Kling | Higgsfield | Adobe AI Tools | Other emerging AI video platforms.


Who can Apply ?

  • Students pursuing Design, Animation, Film, Media, Communication, Advertising, or related fields
  • Self-taught video editors with a strong portfolio are also encouraged to apply.

A strong portfolio / show reel demonstrating editing skills is mandatory.

Portfolio Should Ideally Showcase:


  • Reels / Shorts
  • Performance ads
  • Motion graphics
  • Product videos
  • Social media content
  • AI-generated / AI-assisted videos
  • Before-and-after editing examples
  • Any experimental or trend-based video work


Most importantly, we are looking for someone who can combine editing skills, creativity, social media understanding, and AI experimentation to create videos that are not just visually good but engaging and performance-driven.

jobDescription:
Core AI Engineer Specialist

Experience: 7+ years

Location: Remote


Role Overview:

Experience req can be 7+ years with hands-on work in the pre-transformer era - people who have built models from scratch before 2017 and not just fine-tuned existing models. Good understanding of classical ML/DL algorithms and maths behind it.


We value what you have built over where you studied. A GitHub history, a Kaggle record, merged pull requests to a training library, a paper you reimplemented and evaluated properly all of these count for more with us than the name on your degree. If your CV is thin and your repositories are not, apply anyway. We read the repositories first.


Key Responsibilities:

  • Build models from scratch architectures, training loops, custom losses, data pipelines in PyTorch , not in a wrapper.
  • Post-train language models: supervised fine-tuning, knowledge distillation under a real capacity gap, PEFT, and RL from preferences or verifiable rewards.
  • Implement papers end to end, from an arXiv PDF to working code, and evaluate them rigorously enough that we can act on the result including when it is negative.
  • Adapt general models to specific domains without destroying what they already knew.
  • Cut GPU cost parallelism placement, memory, quantisation, serving-time arithmetic and measure the saving rather than asserting it.
  • Track the field and adopt what is worth adopting, quickly, and tell us what is not.

What we require:

  • Deep learning fundamentals. Backpropagation, optimisation and transformer architectures attention, tokenisation, embeddings understood mechanically, not as vocabulary. You should be able to explain why attention is scaled by 1/d, what a normalisation layer does to gradient flow, and what actually happens in an optimiser step.
  • Hands-on PyTorch or Keras. You build and train models from scratch — not fine-tuning through an API, not Trainer with a config file.
  • LLM post-training, in practice — SFT (data construction, packing, masking, and what goes wrong); knowledge distillation (forward vs reverse KL, on-policy distillation, capacity gaps); PEFT ( LoRA and QLoRA , quantisation, adapter placement and rank selection); RLHF and its descendants — DPO, GRPO, PPO, RLOO : what each optimises and how each fails.
  • Engineering. Solid Python . CUDA and GPU-training basics — what is actually running on the device, and why your step time is what it is. Distributed training (DDP / FSDP) is a plus, not a requirement.
  • Proven ability to implement papers end to end — arXiv to working code — and to evaluate rigorously. Rigorous means seeds, baselines, controls and an honest statement of the noise floor.
  • Speed of adoption. This field moves faster than any curriculum. We need people who read, try, discard and keep the residue — and who can tell the difference between a real advance and a well-marketed one.

Mandatory Tech Stack:

  • Languages: Python, C++, CUDA
  • Deep Learning: PyTorch, NumPy, SciPy
  • LLM / Transformers: Hugging Face Transformers, TRL, Tokenizers
  • Fine-tuning & Post-training: PEFT, LoRA, QLoRA, SFT, DPO, GRPO, PPO, RLOO, Knowledge Distillation
  • Training: DDP, FSDP, DeepSpeed, Mixed Precision, Gradient Checkpointing
  • GPU & Performance: CUDA, NVIDIA GPUs, GPU Profiling, Quantisation, Memory & Compute Optimisation
  • Inference & Serving: vLLM, TensorRT-LLM
  • Data & Experimentation: Hugging Face Datasets, Pandas, Weights & Biases / MLflow
  • Engineering: Linux, Git, GitHub, Docker

Core stack: Python + PyTorch + CUDA + Transformers/TRL + PEFT + LLM Post-training + Distributed Training + GPU Optimisation + vLLM.

title: AI Solutions Analyst
jobDescription:
AI Solutions Analyst

Mumbai Office


About the job

At Nouryon, our global team of changemakers takes positive action every day, to reach higher goals collectively and individually. We create innovative and sustainable solutions for our customers to answer society's needs today and in the future.

The AI Solutions Analyst is a developer on Nouryon's AI invoice intelligence platform an application that reads supplier invoices and extracts charge-level detail to give the business full transparency into logistics cost. This role owns the end-to-end onboarding of vendors onto the platform analysing each vendor's invoice format, engineering the AI instructions that teach the system to read it correctly, and validating extraction quality until it can be trusted. This role is the connective tissue between the digital transformation team, logistics and procurement stakeholders, and the data that drives cost-leakage decisions — ensuring that AI-extracted invoice data translates into measurable savings, organisational transparency, and continuous improvement.


Job Description

The role is centered around the following core pillars:

  • AI Prompt Engineering – Design, tune and test the natural-language instructions that teach the AI to read each vendor's invoice format accurately.
  • Vendor Onboarding – Own the end-to-end onboarding of new vendors onto the platform, from first sample invoice to live, validated extraction.
  • Data Analytics – Serve as the analytical engine of the team by measuring extraction accuracy, error patterns, and AI processing cost, and translating findings into targeted improvements.
  • Data Quality Assurance – Validate AI output against source documents and safeguard the integrity of the invoice data reaching the business.
  • Stakeholder Management – Coordinate with the digital transformation team, logistics procurement, operations, and vendors to align formats, priorities and expectations.
  • Process Improvements – Identify and deploy improvements in onboarding, extraction, and quality-assurance workflows.

Job Responsibilities

Vendor Onboarding & Format Analysis

  • Collect and analyse representative sample invoices from new vendors across warehouse, ocean freight, road/rail, and customs brokerage modes.
  • Identify each vendor's invoice structure, charge-line conventions, and formatting quirks that affect automated extraction.
  • Onboard vendors onto the platform, configuring extraction profiles and routing settings per vendor.
  • Own a named portfolio of vendors end-to-end, from onboarding through to sustained extraction quality.

AI Prompt Engineering & Model Training

  • Design, write and iterate custom extraction prompts that teach the AI to read each vendor's invoices correctly.
  • Test prompt changes against curated reference sets before releasing them to production.
  • Diagnose extraction failures to root cause and resolve them at the prompt level, permanently rather than case by case.
  • Continuously improve extraction accuracy and reduce AI processing cost per invoice.

Validation & Data Quality

  • Validate AI-extracted charge lines, invoice metadata and classifications against source documents until extraction holds reliably.
  • Approve, correct or reject extracted data, ensuring only verified information reaches downstream reporting.
  • Curate golden test sets from verified invoices to support regression testing.
  • Safeguard data quality, completeness and consistency across the vendor portfolio.

Analytics & Performance Reporting

  • Measure and report extraction accuracy, first-pass approval rate, and AI cost per invoice for owned vendors.
  • Analyse error patterns across vendors, modes and document types to identify systemic improvement opportunities.
  • Translate analytical findings into clear, actionable recommendations for the programme team and senior stakeholders.
  • Prepare periodic performance reporting for leadership.

Stakeholder Engagement & Process Improvement

  • Act as a key interface between the digital transformation team, logistics procurement, operations, and vendors on onboarding and extraction topics.
  • Escalate invoice formats or system limitations that require platform-level changes, with a recommended course of action.
  • Identify and implement process improvements across onboarding, prompt engineering, and quality-assurance workflows.
  • Contribute to the continuous improvement of analytics, reporting, and decision-support tooling.

We believe you bring (Education & Experience)

This is a specific profile. We are not looking for a generalist analyst — we are looking for someone who has built AI solutions in the field, against real data, with users watching.

1. Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) experience
You have worked embedded with a business function, not behind a ticket queue. You have taken an ambiguous operational problem, built a working solution against real data, and iterated it in front of the people who use it. You are comfortable when requirements arrive as a conversation rather than a specification.

2. Prompting
You have built something with an LLM that worked measurably better on Friday than it did on Monday — and you can explain exactly why. You treat prompts as engineered artefacts: versioned, tested against a reference set, and improved against a number. Experience with structured extraction from documents is a strong advantage.

3. Scrum
You have delivered in sprints — planning, stand-up, demo, retro — in a self-organising team. This team has no team lead: you will pick up work from a prioritised backlog, commit to it, and be accountable for it without being assigned it.

4. SQL and Python (pandas)
Intermediate SQL: joins, aggregations, grouping, window functions. Python at pandas level, sufficient to analyse extraction results offline, compare model outputs across runs, and quantify accuracy. You use data to prove an improvement, not to describe it.

5. Structured problem decomposition
You turn "this vendor extracts badly" into a specific, testable hypothesis, a defined check, and a fix that holds. You look for the systematic cause behind a single error rather than correcting the symptom.

6. Analytical rigour on documents
You can find one wrong figure in a forty-line charge table — and you are still finding it at four in the afternoon. Sustained precision over high volumes of detailed document work is the daily craft of this role.


Nice to have

  • Domain exposure — finance, procurement, logistics or supply chain; invoices, freight, warehousing, customs (Invoice processing, Accounts Payable)
  • Data annotation, labelling or data-quality operations background
  • Palantir Foundry experience
  • Statistical or ML modelling depth beyond descriptive analytics
  • BI tooling — Power BI, Tableau
  • Scrum certification — CSM / PSM
  • Version control — Git fundamentals
  • Experience supporting European stakeholders from an offshore or captive centre

Education & Experience

  • Bachelor's Degree (BA/BS) in Engineering, Computer Science, Data Science, Supply Chain, Operations Research, or a related field from an accredited institution.

title: Senior Agentic AI Engineer
jobDescription:
Senior Agentic AI Engineer

About the Role

Insurance software implementations are among the most complex, document-heavy, and process-intensive programmes in enterprise technology. A single implementation can involve thousands of configuration decisions, hundreds of requirement documents, and years of delivery time. Sapiens is rebuilding how that work gets done using production-grade AI agents that operate across the full implementation lifecycle, from pre-sales and scoping through to configuration, testing, and go-live.

Work You'll Do

Agent architecture & orchestration

  • Design and implement agentic systems capable of multi-step reasoning, planning, tool use, and workflow execution against complex, document-intensive implementation processes
  • Build stateful workflows using LangGraph or equivalent — including branching, retries, self-correction, human-in-the-loop checkpoints, and reusable orchestration patterns
  • Engineer for long-horizon reliability — multi-step task completion, recovery from compounding errors, planning under uncertainty, and robust tool use when individual steps fail
  • Build the reasoning behind high-stakes implementation decisions — criteria-grounded outputs, structured review patterns, and auditable rationales that delivery consultants can act on and defend

Retrieval, grounding & context engineering

  • Develop end-to-end RAG pipelines: ingestion, chunking, embeddings, vector and hybrid retrieval, reranking, contextual compression, and grounding strategies
  • Engineer memory and context management — conversational state, persistent memory, retrieval-aware context assembly, and token-efficient context selection
  • Apply MCP-style tool and context interfaces so agents access the right information at the right time across enterprise knowledge repositories, document sources, and structured configuration data

Reliability, evaluation & safety

  • Implement observability and tracing for prompts, tool calls, retrieval quality, agent traces, failures, drift, latency, and production behaviour
  • Apply guardrails, safety controls, and failure-handling to reduce hallucinations in agents whose outputs practitioners act on directly in live client settings
  • Evaluate agents at trajectory and task level — multi-step task success, failure-mode and regression analysis, sandboxed test environments — alongside retrieval and generation quality metrics, automated checks, and human review

Integration & production craft

  • Build integrations with internal and external tools, APIs, enterprise systems, databases, and model providers so agents operate reliably within real delivery workflows
  • Deliver production-quality Python code with strong practices in testing, CI/CD, logging, versioning, and documentation; make architecture decisions that balance quality, reliability, latency, cost, and model risk
  • Translate ambiguous, high-complexity implementation processes into robust system logic and reusable AI patterns; stay current with advances in agentic systems and translate research into practical engineering decisions

Required Qualifications

  • Demonstrated depth building and shipping production agentic AI systems — we weigh shipped systems over years in a title
  • Strong, hands-on experience with LangGraph or equivalent agentic orchestration frameworks, including custom orchestration
  • Deep proficiency in Python — clean, testable, production-ready code
  • Experience designing and optimising end-to-end RAG systems: indexing, retrieval, reranking, grounding, and evaluation
  • Daily working proficiency with Claude (Anthropic API) and Claude Code — you use these tools every day, not occasionally
  • Experience building and deploying agents on Azure AI Foundry or an equivalent enterprise cloud AI platform
  • Practical understanding of LLM behaviour — strengths, limitations, hallucination risks, reasoning constraints, and the evaluation methods used to measure them
  • Experience evaluating and debugging agent behaviour at trajectory and task level, not just output quality
  • Hands-on experience with MCP-based interoperability patterns and tool-calling agent design
  • Modern software practices: testing, CI/CD, observability, tracing, and debugging for LLM-based systems in production

Preferred Qualifications

jobDescription:
Job Summary
Bajaj Finserv Web is a critical component of the company's omnipresence strategy. You will be working with India's largest NBFC's web technology stack, encompassing over 40 business lines and 230+ features, with nearly 500 million traffic and managing over 30,000 webpages. It is an integrated platform offering a portfolio of products covering payments, cards, wallets, loans, deposits, mutual funds, and loans on lifestyle products, ranging from consumer durables to home furnishings. The Software Development Manager (SDM) - Full Stack leads a single POD of 5-7 developers building the experience and services layer of this platform on Next.js, React and Node JS. Reporting to the Technical Architect - Frontend, the role converts approved architecture and design system standards into production-grade full stack implementations - server rendered and statically generated pages, shared components, BFF and API integration layers - and is accountable for the POD's delivery predictability, Core Web Vitals, code quality and compliance posture. The role is expected to remain hands-on, conduct code reviews, enforce engineering standards and SOPs, and continuously raise the productivity of the POD through automation and AI-assisted engineering.
Responsibilities
  • Data Privacy and Security: Ensure all development within the POD complies with applicable data privacy regulation, RBI and internal information security policy, including data localisation requirements for any cloud or AI service used.
  • Secure SDLC: Enforce secure coding practices covering the OWASP Top 10, dependency and supply chain scanning, secrets management, and timely closure of VAPT and application security findings.
  • Browser and Client Security: Ensure correct implementation of CSP, XSS and CSRF protection, secure token and session handling in the browser, and governance of third-party scripts and tags on the POD's surfaces.
  • Audit Readiness: Maintain traceability from requirement to code to release - approvals, change records, test evidence and deployment records - so that internal audit and regulatory reviews can be served without rework.
  • Incident Management: Own the POD's participation in production incident response, root cause analysis and preventive action tracking, ensuring minimal customer impact.
  • Innovation and Engineering Productivity: Execute POCs to validate frameworks, rendering approaches and migration paths with clear benchmarking on performance, cost and scalability before adoption.
  • Innovation and Engineering Productivity: Drive adoption of AI-assisted and agentic engineering within the POD - code generation, review assistance, test generation and design-to-code workflows - with measurable impact on velocity and quality and with clear guardrails on data, IP and security.
  • Innovation and Engineering Productivity: Support the migration of the existing CMS rendered estate to a composable Next.js frontend for the POD's scope, ensuring zero regression on organic traffic, analytics and compliance sensitive journeys.
  • Innovation and Engineering Productivity: Leverage and sponsor innovation work through internal incubators and the external start-up network to introduce novel technical capabilities into the platform.
  • Core Development and Delivery: Maintain a technical debt and dependency upgrade register for the POD's codebase with an agreed remediation plan, including supply chain risk across the dependency tree.
  • Core Development and Delivery: Establish frontend observability for the POD - real user monitoring, synthetic checks and error tracking through New Relic, Datadog and Lighthouse CI - and act on the telemetry.
  • POD and Team Management: Technical Mentorship: Provide day to day technical guidance to 5-7 developers, run design and code walkthroughs, and build depth in the POD through structured learning paths and pair programming.
  • POD and Team Management: Performance Management: Set clear, measurable goals for every team member, conduct regular one-on-ones and reviews, give constructive feedback, and close the appraisal cycle within timelines.

  • POD and Team Management: Talent Acquisition and Retention: Participate in hiring panels, own the technical evaluation of candidates for the POD, and run structured onboarding and ramp-up plans for new joiners, byte hires and partner resources.
  • POD and Team Management: Partner Management: Manage in-POD vendor and partner developers to the same standard of quality, hygiene and delivery discipline as internal engineers.
  • POD and Team Management: Team Collaboration: Build a cohesive POD with strong communication into Product, Design, Content, QA and infrastructure teams, and maintain high engagement and morale.
  • Core Development and Delivery: Own end-to-end delivery for the POD - sprint planning, estimation, build, code review, testing, release and post-release stabilisation - for all web and in-app surfaces in scope.
  • Core Development and Delivery: Translate the solution design provided by the Technical Architect into implementable low-level designs, component specifications, API and data contracts, and task breakdowns for the POD.
  • Core Development and Delivery: Remain hands-on for a meaningful share of the role (target 30-40%) on Next.js and React development with TypeScript, including App Router, React Server Components, SSR, SSG, ISR and streaming.
  • Core Development and Delivery: Own the POD's Node JS services and BFF layer - route handlers, API aggregation, GraphQL and REST consumption, caching, resilience patterns, timeouts and error handling.
  • Core Development and Delivery: Consume and contribute to the enterprise design system and shared component library, ensuring token, theming, versioning and Storybook discipline rather than local forks and one-off components.
  • Core Development and Delivery: Implement integration with headless content sources (AEM headless or other CMS/DXP), commerce and backend services through the contract layer defined by the Architect.
  • Core Development and Delivery: Own state management, data fetching and form and validation architecture within the POD's applications, keeping patterns consistent with the platform standard.
  • Core Development and Delivery: Own edge and caching behaviour for the POD's routes in partnership with CDN teams - cache key design, revalidation, purge strategy and origin protection across Akamai and Cloudflare.
  • Core Development and Delivery: Drive release readiness through build checklists, feature flag and progressive rollout plans, deployment runbooks, rollback plans and production hypercare for every deployment.
  • Core Development and Delivery: Ensure the POD's digital assets continue to perform through peak sales season by designing for auto-scale, graceful degradation and resilient rendering across the Node / SSR tier, CDN and origin.
  • Engineering Quality and Performance Governance: Define and enforce coding standards, branching strategy, peer review, merge and promotion discipline across the POD using Git, GitHub Actions or Jenkins, and monorepo and package governance conventions.
  • Engineering Quality and Performance Governance: Own quality gates - SonarQube, static analysis, code coverage, bundle size checks, Lighthouse CI budgets and automated security scanning - and hold the line on defect density and escaped defects.
  • Engineering Quality and Performance Governance: Own the POD's Core Web Vitals outcomes (LCP, INP, CLS) including bundle analysis and code splitting, image and font strategy, hydration cost, streaming and partial prerendering, with explicit optimisation for low-end Android devices, low bandwidth networks and in-app webviews.
  • Engineering Quality and Performance Governance: Ensure testing coverage across unit, component, contract and end-to-end layers using Jest, Testing Library, Playwright or Cypress, along with visual regression, before any release is certified.
  • Engineering Quality and Performance Governance: Own SEO, GEO, structured data, render parity and accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA) as build-time concerns for the POD rather than post-release corrections.
Key Decisions / Dimensions
  • Following decisions are taken by the role:
  • Low-level design and component design decisions within the boundaries of the architecture and design system standards approved by the Technical Architect.
  • Rendering mode selection per route - SSR, SSG, ISR or client rendering - within the strategy defined by the Architect.
  • Implementation approach for BFF and API integration, state management, error handling and resilience patterns for the POD's scope.
  • Sprint scope, story sequencing, estimation and allocation of work across the 5-7 developers in the POD

Performance Marketing

SEO Organic Growth

  • Support SEO requirements for new website pages, blogs, case studies, and other content.

PR Brand Visibility

Content Proofreading

jobDescription:
Job Summary

We are seeking a hands-on Manager - Global Accounting, Consolidation Reporting to own the month-end close, multi-entity consolidation, and reporting for a fast-growing consumer and technology company operating across 8+ legal entities (US, India, UK, Canada, China, Hong Kong, and 4 new EU entities launching soon).

This role reports to the Director of Accounting and manages a team of 4 (Sheeba, Saurabh, and 2 new hires - Sr GL Analyst and FA Analyst). You will own the T+3 soft / T+6 hard / T+7 reporting close cadence, group consolidation, forex restatement, payroll accounting, intercompany, equity accounting (SBC/ESOPs), and audit coordination with Deloitte (US) and local firms.

The ideal candidate is a qualified Chartered Accountant with 8-10 years of post-qualification experience running global US GAAP close, comfortable owning technical accounting judgments, and ready to build accounting maturity as the company scales into new geographies.

You will work closely with the Finance Controller, VP Accounting (US), FPA, Payroll Director, Tax Lead, and external auditors.

Success in this role means an on-time, accurate close every month across all entities, clean audits, strong internal financial controls, and a team that grows with you.

Responsibilities

  • Own the global month-end, quarter-end, and year-end close cadence: T+3 soft / T+6 hard / T+7 reporting across all 11+ entities.
  • Own multi-entity consolidation and elimination entries, including forex restatement across 8+ base currencies (USD, INR, GBP, CAD, CNY, HKD, EUR).
  • Own intercompany transactions between US parent and all subsidiaries, including cross-entity postings, netting, and transfer pricing entries in coordination with the Tax Lead.
  • Own Fixed Assets accounting (across all entities) until the FA Analyst is hired; then transition to review-only.
  • Own end-to-end statutory and regulatory compliance for the accounting function across three regions - Europe (UK + Germany, Spain, Netherlands, France) - including books-and-records compliance, statutory filings, statutory audits, and coordination with local consultants and regulators. Partner with the Tax Lead on tax-specific filings.
  • Lead the annual audit with local audit firms across 6+ geographies. Own PBC lists, coordination, and audit deliverables.
  • Own all payroll accounting reconciliations across geographies (13+ recurring recs: Salaries, Bonus, PF, ESI, PT, Medical, Dental, Vision, Withholding, Gratuity, Leave Encashment, NPS, Commissions).
  • Manage a team of 3-4 direct reports.
  • Drive process improvements in close, consolidation, and reporting - reduce close timeline, improve accuracy, automate wherever possible.

Requirements

  • Chartered Accountant (CA) with 8-10 years of post-qualification experience.
  • At least 4-5 years managing a global accounting team in a multi-entity, multi-currency environment.
  • Deep, hands-on US GAAP expertise (ASC 606, ASC 842, SBC, consolidation, revenue recognition).
  • Experience with NetSuite (OneWorld, Multi-Book) is required. Working knowledge of Coupa (AP), Numeric (close management), Avalara (tax), Carta (equity) is a strong plus.
  • Experience owning close + consolidation across 5+ legal entities and multiple base currencies.
  • Big 4 background (Deloitte, PwC, EY, KPMG) preferred. Prior experience at a fast-growing consumer or tech company preferred.
  • Hands-on experience managing statutory and regulatory compliance across multiple jurisdictions (US, India, Europe). Familiarity with US GAAP and local GAAPs (Ind AS, F/ IFRS for UK, EU-country local GAAPs).
  • Working knowledge of India tax regimes (GST, TDS, corporate tax), US sales tax + federal filings, and EU VAT / intra-EU compliance strongly preferred.
  • Strong people leadership skills; ability to coach analysts and grow a team.
  • Strong problem-solving, ownership, and stakeholder management (US-based leadership + external auditors).
  • Comfort in a fast-moving environment with expanding geographic footprint (EU launch imminent).

jobDescription:
Why This Role Exists

Jira Service Management has evolved into a critical enterprise platform supporting IT Asset Management, Vulnerability Management, Incident Management, Change Management, and key operational workflows. Recent regulatory examinations and our cybersecurity program have reinforced the importance of maintaining a complete and accurate IT asset inventory the foundation for vulnerability management, incident response, disaster recovery, and regulatory reporting.

To date, the platform has been maintained by team members as part of broader responsibilities. As its scope and strategic importance have grown, we now require dedicated expertise and capacity to maintain the platform, develop integrations with systems such as automated asset discovery, enhance workflows, and ensure ongoing data quality. A dedicated ITSM Platform Engineer will own this critical platform reducing operational risk, improving automation and efficiency, and ensuring the reliable asset and operational data needed to support regulatory expectations and our cybersecurity strategy.

Job Purpose

We are seeking an experienced Jira Administrator / JSM Engineer to own the administration, configuration, governance, and ongoing support of Jira Software, Jira Service Management (JSM), and Confluence. This role serves as the primary platform administrator responsible for designing and maintaining workflows, forms, automation, asset-management processes, service catalogs, reporting, and integrations that support Technology, Operations, Security, and Business teams across the enterprise. The ideal candidate combines strong technical administration skills with process expertise in Asset Management (Asset Inventory), Incident Management, Change Management, Service Request Management, and Agile delivery practices.

Key Responsibilities

Atlassian Platform Administration

  • Administer and maintain Jira Software, Jira Service Management (JSM), and Confluence.
  • Configure and manage projects, issue types, workflows, screens, custom fields, permissions, notification schemes, and security roles.
  • Maintain platform health, performance, reliability, and data integrity.
  • Implement platform governance standards, naming conventions, and configuration best practices.
  • Manage user provisioning, licensing, access controls, and security configurations.

Jira Service Management (JSM)

  • Configure and maintain JSM service desks, queues, request types, SLAs, customer portals, and service catalogs.
  • Design and enhance Incident Management, Change Management, Problem Management, and Service Request workflows.
  • Build and maintain incident, problem, change, release, and operational-support forms.
  • Configure approval workflows, escalation paths, notifications, and service-level management processes.
  • Partner with Production Support, Infrastructure, Security, and Application teams to optimize ITSM processes.

Assets & Configuration Management

  • Administer Jira Service Management Assets (CMDB).
  • Design and maintain asset schemas, object types, relationships, and data models.
  • Develop processes for managing hardware, software, cloud resources, applications, and technology assets.
  • Establish asset lifecycle management processes including onboarding, changes, audits, and retirement.
  • Implement integrations between Assets and incident, change, and service-request processes.
  • Ensure asset data quality, governance, and reporting accuracy.

Workflow Configuration & Automation

  • Design, develop, and maintain Jira workflows that support business and technology processes.
  • Configure automation rules to streamline approvals, notifications, escalations, and repetitive tasks.
  • Develop and support integrations with enterprise tools and external systems.
  • Drive continuous-improvement initiatives that improve operational efficiency and reduce manual effort.

Reporting & Analytics

  • Build and maintain dashboards, reports, KPIs, and executive metrics.
  • Provide reporting on incident trends, SLA performance, change effectiveness, asset compliance, and operational health.
  • Develop meaningful analytics that support management decision-making and process improvements.

User Support & Enablement

  • Serve as the primary escalation point for Jira and JSM platform issues.
  • Provide user training, documentation, and best-practice guidance.
  • Partner with stakeholders to capture requirements and deliver platform enhancements.
  • Support onboarding of new teams and business units onto the Atlassian platform.

Required Qualifications

  • 5+ years of hands-on Jira administration experience.
  • 3+ years of experience administering Jira Service Management (JSM).
  • Strong experience configuring: Jira workflows; screens and issue types; custom fields; permission schemes; notification schemes; SLAs and queues; customer portals; automation rules.
  • Experience implementing and administering JSM Assets / CMDB solutions.
  • Strong understanding of Incident Management, Change Management, Problem Management, Service Request Management, and ITSM best practices.
  • Experience with Confluence administration and knowledge management.
  • Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellentcommunication and stakeholder-management abilities.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Atlassian Certified Professional certifications.
  • Experience with ScriptRunner, Automation for Jira, and Marketplace plugins.
  • Experience integrating Jira with monitoring, CI/CD, identity management, and cloud platforms.
  • Knowledge of ITIL best practices.
  • Experience supporting enterprise-scale Jira environments.
  • Experience with Agile, Scrum, and Kanban methodologies.

What the Client Expects

  • Full ownership of the Atlassian platform not task-by-task support, but end-to-end accountability for configuration, governance, and data quality.
  • Reliable daily overlap with US Eastern business hours and clear, proactive written and verbal English communication with US teams.
  • Ability to work independently, translate business/technology requirements into working configuration, and deliver enhancements with minimal hand-holding.
  • A governance-first mindset: accurate CMDB/asset data, auditable change processes, and reporting that stands up to regulatory examination.

Eizen AI is an applied AI company building computer vision, video intelligence, and agentic AI systems for enterprises. We work with Fortune 500 organisations across manufacturing, retail, healthcare, and robotics, turning real-world video and operational data into decisions that run in production not in slide decks.
Our platform stack includes eizenOS, our video intelligence platform for large-scale perception and analytics, and eizenX, our agentic workflow design layer for building and orchestrating AI agents. Alongside these, our proprietary Dual Vision System combines ego-vision and exo-vision to give robotic and industrial systems a far richer operational understanding of their environment than single-viewpoint approaches allow.
Eizen operates from Hyderabad our primary R&D centre with a growing presence in Bengaluru and Atlanta, USA. We are a research-led team: our work sits at the intersection of self-supervised learning for video, visual symbol grounding, and production-grade AI engineering. About This Role
Eizen is expanding its engineering team to support a major client engagement focused on building and scaling AI products. You will own full-stack product modules end to end React + TypeScript on the frontend, Python + FastAPI on the backend and the agentic AI layer that sits between them.
This is a genuinely full-stack role with an AI centre of gravity. Agent orchestration, tool execution, and retrieval pipelines are not a side project here; they are the product. That brings engineering problems most web teams never encounter: long-running multi-step workflows, non-deterministic model output, partial failures mid-execution, streaming responses, and retrieval quality that has to be measured rather than assumed. You will design for those conditions across the stack from the UI that streams a response to the worker that retries a failed tool call.
We are looking for an engineer who takes a module from architecture through production and stays accountable for it: contracts, data model, performance, tests, observability, and the go-get-things done behaviour.

About the Role

Insurance software implementations are among the most complex, document-heavy, and process-intensive programmes in enterprise technology. Sapiens is rebuilding how that work gets done using production-grade AI agents that operate across the full implementation lifecycle, from pre-sales and scoping through to configuration, testing, and go-live.

Agent architecture & orchestration

Technical Program Manager (TPM)

Role Overview
The Technical Program Manager (TPM) drives complex technical programs from planning through execution and delivery.
At redBus, TPMs are expected to be technical leaders, execution drivers, and force multipliers who bring clarity to ambiguity, improve delivery predictability, and use AI and automation to make teams more effective.
Whether you're helping launch new features, scaling core backend APIs, setting up regional compliance, or introducing new AI capabilities, you will be the key collaborative partner who connects the dots, resolves cross-team dependencies, and keeps everyone moving forward smoothly.


Key Responsibilities
Program Delivery
  • Cross-Domain Leadership: Lead complex technical programs, geo-expansions, and cross-functional initiatives across the organization.
  • Goal Translation : Translate business goals into clear plans, milestones, ownership, and measurable outcomes.
  • Proactive Risk Management : Identify risks, dependencies, and blockers early and drive mitigation plans to closure.

  • Release Readiness : Drive release readiness and confidence across Engineering, QA, Infrastructure, Product, and Operations.
  • Stakeholder Governance : Communicate program health, risks, decisions, and trade-offs clearly to stakeholders and leadership.

  • Continuous Improvement: Improve planning, execution, governance, and cross-team collaboration through data-driven interventions and post-sprint RCAs.
AI Program Leadership

  • Collaborative Formulation: Partner with Product, Engineering, Data, and ML teams to define scope, execution plans, and success metrics.
  • AI Success Metrics: Track AI-specific performance metrics, including model accuracy, latency, reliability, token costs, and adoption.
  • Safety & Quality Guardrails: Ensure AI solutions consider privacy, data security, model quality, continuous monitoring, and graceful fallback mechanisms.
AI, Automation & Tooling (Internal Productivity)
  • Agile Tooling Innovation: Build or prototype lightweight tools, dashboards, automations, and AI-powered workflows to optimize program tracking.
  • Process Automation: Use AI to improve requirement analysis, risk detection, dependency tracking, reporting, and release readiness.

  • Scalable Mechanisms: Identify manual operational processes that can be replaced with scalable automation.


Qualifications

  • Proactive Mitigation: Identifies and resolves risks before they turn into blockers.

  • Scripting skills using Shell, REXX, or CLIST
  • Experience in vendor coordination and defect resolution
  • Demonstrated leadership in enterprise mainframe operations

Preferred Technical and Professional Experience

  • Hands-on experience with IBM Tivoli, OMEGAMON, NetView, and System Automation tools
  • Proven capability in mainframe automation, self-healing platform implementation, and AIOps-driven observability integration
  • Familiarity with DevOps practices for mainframe environments and hybrid cloud integration
  • Knowledge of z/OS security products such as RACF, ACF2, and Top Secret
  • Experience in capacity forecasting and enterprise optimization strategies
  • Exposure to modernization and transformation programs and defining enterprise operational standards
  • Experience with modern automation frameworks such as Ansible and Zowe
  • Understanding of mainframe API enablement and integration technologies
  • Knowledge of compliance, audit frameworks, and ITIL-based service management practices
  • Cross-platform infrastructure integration experience
  • Strong mentoring, technical leadership, and stakeholder management capabilities
  • Focus on continuous improvement and operational excellence initiatives

jobDescription:
Production AI Needs More Than Models: Why Enterprise Infrastructure Is Becoming the New Competitive Advantage

Enterprise AI has entered a new phase.

For the past two years, organizations have focused on experimentation testing copilots, evaluating foundation models, building proofs of concept, and exploring new use cases. Public cloud played a critical role in enabling this wave of innovation, providing rapid access to compute, models, and AI services.

But production AI is fundamentally different from AI experimentation.

When AI becomes embedded in business operations, customer experiences, internal workflows, and decision-making systems, infrastructure choices become strategic business decisions. Questions about cost, governance, data ownership, integration, and operational control move from the IT department to the boardroom.

Recent research from Broadcom s Private Cloud Outlook 2026 highlights this shift. Based on a survey of 1,800 senior IT decision-makers worldwide, the report found that 56% of organizations are running or planning to run production AI inference in private cloud environments, while public cloud use for production inference declined from 56% to 41% year over year.

The message is not that public cloud is disappearing.

The message is that enterprises are becoming far more intentional about where AI workloads run and why.

At Kirk Tech Solutions, we believe this represents a larger transition:

The next phase of enterprise AI will be defined not only by access to models, but by ownership of the infrastructure, data, governance, and operations that make AI work at scale.

AI Is Becoming an Infrastructure Challenge

The first generation of enterprise AI projects often focused on models:

  • Which LLM should we use
  • Should we use a hosted API or open-weight models
  • Which AI platform is best

These remain important questions.

But as organizations move from pilots to production, new questions emerge:

  • How do we control infrastructure costs
  • Where does enterprise data reside
  • How do we govern AI systems
  • How do we integrate AI into existing operations
  • How do we scale securely

These are infrastructure questions.

Broadcom s research suggests that enterprises are already adjusting. Security, cost predictability, performance, sovereignty requirements, and operational control are increasingly influencing workload-placement decisions.

This shift is particularly important for AI inference.

Unlike experimentation, production inference can create sustained demand for compute, storage, networking, GPUs, monitoring, security, and data movement. AI systems often operate against sensitive information and become integrated into business-critical processes.

As AI moves deeper into operations, enterprises need more than models.

They need production-ready infrastructure.

The Economics of AI Are Changing Cloud Strategy

One of the most significant findings in the Broadcom report is the growing concern around cloud economics.

For the first time, cost overtook security as the top public cloud challenge. The report found that 97% of IT leaders believe some portion of their public cloud spending is wasted, and more than half estimate that waste exceeds 25% of total cloud spend.

AI amplifies this challenge.

Inference workloads increase demand for:

  • GPU capacity
  • High-performance storage
  • Data transfer
  • Network bandwidth
  • Security tooling
  • Observability platforms
  • Model serving infrastructure

The issue is not that public cloud lacks value. Public cloud remains highly effective for experimentation, elastic workloads, and specialized services.

However, enterprises are increasingly evaluating whether sustained AI workloads require a different operating model one that offers greater predictability and tighter alignment between infrastructure investment and business outcomes.

This is one reason workload repatriation is accelerating.

Broadcom found that 50% of enterprises have already moved some workloads from public cloud to private environments, while 33% are considering repatriation meaning 83% have either already repatriated workloads or are considering doing so. Notably, AI training, large language models, and inference appeared as a repatriation category for the first time in the 2026 research.

This is not a rejection of public cloud.

It is the emergence of a workload-centric strategy: placing each workload where it performs best economically, operationally, and securely.

Data Sovereignty Is Becoming an AI Requirement

AI introduces another challenge that extends beyond infrastructure economics: control.

AI systems increasingly interact with:

  • Customer information
  • Financial data
  • Intellectual property
  • Operational systems
  • Internal knowledge repositories
  • Regulated data

As organizations deploy AI into core business processes, they need visibility into:

  • Where data resides
  • Who can access it
  • Where models execute
  • How information moves
  • Which policies apply

Broadcom found that data sovereignty and residency requirements are now the leading geopolitical factor influencing IT strategy, cited by 54% of respondents. Four out of five IT leaders say geopolitical and regulatory concerns are affecting infrastructure decisions.

This is particularly relevant as enterprises move toward agentic AI systems capable of accessing tools, triggering workflows, and interacting with business applications.

Governance cannot be an afterthought.

It must be built into the architecture from the beginning.

Where FlatClaw Fits Into the Private AI Equation

As enterprise AI evolves from chatbots to AI coworkers and agentic systems, infrastructure becomes increasingly important. These systems can access enterprise knowledge, work with files, interact with applications, invoke tools, and automate workflows.

AI is no longer simply generating answers it can become part of how the enterprise operates. That makes data, security, governance, cost, and infrastructure ownership strategic considerations.

FlatClaw: Private AI Built for Enterprise Control

FlatClaw Private AI Coworker Platform is an open-source, private-cloud platform designed for private, single-tenant deployments within a customer s dedicated environment.

Its architecture emphasizes:

  • Customer-owned cloud deployment
  • Dedicated cloud or bare-metal infrastructure
  • Single-tenant architecture
  • Dedicated GPU infrastructure
  • Predictable infrastructure economics
  • Data remaining within the customer s environment
  • Persistent organizational AI memory
  • Enterprise integrations and RBAC
  • Open, auditable frameworks

FlatClaw also supports integrations such as Google Workspace and Jira, along with custom MCP protocols.

From AI Consumption to AI Ownership

As AI becomes more deeply embedded in enterprise operations, organizations need to think beyond model subscriptions and API consumption.

They need to ask:

Who controls the infrastructure, data, deployment, compute, economics, and auditability of their AI

title: Griffin Club - Communications Lead
jobDescription:
Inc42 is India s #1 startup media intelligence platform that informs, educates and empowers startup business leaders through its incisive reporting, insightful reports, curated Events Conferences communities, and industry-leading executive courses programs.

Since launching in January 2015 and having risen to become the authoritative voice on India s startup economy, weve moved markets, gotten the early scoop on billions of dollars of transactions, and told you whats happening deep inside some of the fastest-growing startups industries alike.

Our stories have been followed by the Wall Street Journal, Bloomberg, Reuters, TechCrunch, and other major outlets hundreds of times. We also track over 10,000+ startups and provide market research and intelligence through our in-depth research reports, and we organise some of the most sought-after conferences and Events for startup business leaders across India.


The Inc42 Impact
  • Inc42 stories reach over 50 Mn+ people monthly
  • Published more than 55,000 stories
  • Successfully conducted 125+ events
  • Launched 100+ research reports
  • Receives 500+ startup applications monthly
  • Worked with 350+ brands
Griffin is a private, invitation-only club that unites India s top tech founders through curated experiences, strategic learning, and peer-driven growth. Designed for India s unicorn and soonicorn founders - building at scale, Griffin offers a trusted space where founders don t just network-they forge deep, meaningful relationships, share unfiltered insights, and collaborate to shape India s next chapter of innovation.

From intimate salons and high-trust retreats to access to capital and exclusive opportunities, Griffin offers a curated path to clarity, collaboration, and personal growth. More than a community, it s the inner circle powering the next wave of industry-shaping leaders.

Job Overview
  • At Griffin, communication is not content creation - it is trust-building at the highest level.
  • As the Communication Lead, Griffin Club, you will own the voice, narrative, and communication engine of one of India s most exclusive founder collectives. This role sits at the intersection of brand, founder relationships, government engagement, member communication, event communication, and institutional storytelling.
  • You will work closely with the Founder s Office and Griffin leadership to ensure that every message going out of Griffin - whether to a unicorn founder, a minister s office, a public-market leader, a global institution, a member, a partner, or an internal team - feels sharp, thoughtful, premium, and worthy of the Griffin room.
  • This is not a conventional communications role. You are not just writing posts, invites, emails, or updates. You are helping shape how India s most consequential founders are spoken to, how Griffin is perceived, and how high-trust relationships are built through language, nuance, discretion, and speed.
  • This role is built for someone with exceptional writing ability, strong judgment, high ownership, and a deep bias for action.

Your Impact In This Role
  • Shape Griffin s Voice: Define and maintain the communication tone for Griffin across founder outreach, member updates, event invites, government notes, institutional communication, and brand narratives.
  • Work With India s Top Founders: Write and manage communication for a private room of unicorn, soonicorn, IPO-bound, and listed company founders.
  • Drive High-Stakes Outreach: Support communication with founders, investors, government offices, embassies, public-market leaders, institutions, and strategic partners.
  • Build Founder-First Narratives: Translate Griffin s work into crisp, sharp, emotionally intelligent communication that feels premium, private, and high-signal.
  • Power Griffin Events Experiences: Own communication before, during, and after Griffin Salons, Retreats, IPO Dialogues, international delegations, private dinners, and institutional engagements.
  • Create Speed With Quality: Build systems, templates, message banks, briefing notes, follow-ups, and communication processes that help Griffin move faster without losing nuance.
Primary Responsibilities
1. Griffin Brand Communication
  • Own Griffin s written voice across all key external and internal touchpoints.
  • Build and maintain Griffin s communication principles, tone guidelines, messaging banks, and standard templates.
  • Draft sharp and premium communication for Griffin announcements, member introductions, founder stories, event positioning, post-event notes, and institutional narratives.
  • Ensure all Griffin communication feels discreet, founder-first, high-trust, and never mass-market or sales-led.
  • Work closely with the design and events teams to ensure that visual communication and written communication feel aligned.
  • Support website copy, brochure copy, event collateral, invite text, membership communication, and presentation narratives.
2. Founder Outreach Prospect Communication
  • Draft founder outreach messages, warm introductions, follow-ups, membership notes, and invite communication.
  • Personalise communication for high-value founders depending on their company stage, sector, public profile, and relationship context.
  • Support communication for new member onboarding, application follow-ups, renewal conversations, and membership value communication.
  • Create crisp founder briefs and context notes before important calls or meetings.
  • Ensure founder-facing communication is thoughtful, respectful, direct, and never generic.
  • Maintain a bank of high-quality outreach formats for different founder segments - listed founders, IPO-bound founders, unicorn founders, exited founders, global founders, and ecosystem leaders.
3. Member Communication
  • Own regular member-facing communication across WhatsApp, email, event invites, updates, reminders, thank-you notes, and post-event follow-ups.
  • Draft new member introductions for the Griffin WhatsApp group in a sharp, credible, and premium format.
  • Write birthday notes, milestone notes, congratulatory messages, founder achievements, IPO updates, funding updates, and other member moments.
  • Ensure every member touchpoint feels personal, considered, and aligned with the stature of the room.
  • Work with the team to maintain updated member profiles, founder context, communication history, and relationship notes.
  • Support renewal communication by helping articulate value delivered to members over the year.
4. Event Communication
  • Own communication for Griffin Retreats, Salons, IPO Dialogues, private dinners, institutional rooms, international delegations, and closed-door founder gatherings.
  • Draft event save-the-dates, invitations, agenda notes, speaker invites, moderator briefs, attendee notes, reminders, and post-event thank-you messages.
  • Create high-quality communication for speakers, founders, partners, government offices, institutional guests, and internal teams.
  • Work closely with the events and operations teams to ensure communication is timely, accurate, and aligned with event flow.
  • Prepare pre-event briefing notes for founders, moderators, speakers, and VIP guests.
  • Capture post-event highlights and convert them into founder-safe summaries, internal notes, and premium archival material.
5. Government, Institutional Strategic Communication
  • Draft communication for government reach-outs, embassy interactions, policy stakeholders, regulators, public-market institutions, exchanges, global institutions, and strategic partners.
  • Support Griffin leadership with high-stakes emails, formal letters, meeting notes, briefing documents, and thank-you communication.
  • Write in a tone that is diplomatic, polished, respectful, and appropriate for senior stakeholders.
  • Help position Griffin as a credible soft-power platform for India s leading technology founders.
  • Maintain communication quality for institutional engagements in India and abroad.
  • Ensure sensitive communication is handled with discretion, context, and maturity.
6. Content Systems, Documentation Communication Infrastructure
  • Build Griffin s internal communication repository - message banks, invite templates, founder introduction formats, thank-you notes, government note formats, event copy formats, and briefing structures.
  • Document communication learnings after major events and outreach campaigns.
  • Maintain a communication tracker for important outreach, pending replies, follow-ups, and next steps.
  • Create repeatable systems so that high-quality communication does not depend only on last-minute drafting.
  • Use AI tools intelligently to improve speed, research, first drafts, summaries, and versioning - while ensuring all final communication has human judgment and Griffin-level taste.
  • Bring structure to ambiguity and convert scattered context into clear, usable communication.
7. Cross-Functional Collaboration
  • Work closely with the Founder s Office, events team, design team, partnerships team, finance team, and leadership team.
  • Convert inputs from different stakeholders into clear, sharp, action-ready communication.
  • Push for clarity wherever needed - audience, objective, tone, timing, CTA, and follow-up.
  • Ensure communication is not created in isolation but supports Griffin s broader goals across acquisition, retention, experience, access, partnerships, and brand.
  • Be proactive in identifying communication gaps before they become execution gaps.

What Sets You Apart
  • Exceptional Writing Ability: You can write with clarity, elegance, sharpness, and restraint. You know the difference between premium communication and verbose communication.
  • Bias For Action: You do not wait endlessly for perfect inputs. You move fast, create strong first drafts, ask the right questions, and push things to closure.
  • Founder-First Sensibility: You understand how to speak to senior founders without sounding transactional, salesy, casual, or overawed.
  • Diplomatic Judgment: You know how to write to senior government officials, investors, institutions, and public figures with maturity and nuance.
  • High Ownership: You take complete responsibility for communication outcomes - from first draft to final send-out to follow-up.
  • Strategic Thinking: You do not just write words. You understand the objective behind the message, the relationship context, and the desired outcome.
  • Taste Restraint: You know what not to say. You can make communication feel premium, sparse, warm, and intentional.
  • Comfort With Ambiguity: You can work with incomplete context and still create structure, direction, and quality output.
  • Ecosystem Fluency: You understand, or are deeply curious about, India s startup, venture capital, public markets, policy, and founder ecosystem.
  • High EQ Discretion: You can handle sensitive conversations, private founder information, and high-trust relationships with maturity.
  • Process Orientation: You can build templates, systems, trackers, and documentation so that communication improves over time.
  • Curiosity-Led Mindset: You like understanding people, companies, sectors, public profiles, business journeys, and the context behind relationships.

Professional Traits
  • 3-4 years of experience in communications, founder s office, public relations, corporate communications, policy communication, investor relations, journalism, or ecosystem-facing roles.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to write across formats - WhatsApp messages, emails, formal letters, event invites, briefing notes, speaker invites, founder introductions, post-event notes, and internal documents.
  • Prior experience working with founders, CXOs, investors, government stakeholders, media houses, public institutions, premium communities, or high-trust networks is preferred.
  • Strong understanding of India s startup ecosystem, founder journeys, public markets, venture capital, policy, and technology sectors is a strong advantage.
  • Ability to synthesise scattered inputs into crisp, high-quality communication.
  • Strong stakeholder management skills and comfort working with senior internal and external stakeholders.
  • Ability to operate in a fast-moving environment where priorities can shift quickly.
  • Strong command over tone - warm when needed, formal when needed, sharp when needed, and diplomatic when needed.
  • Comfort using AI tools for drafting, research, summarisation, versioning, and communication workflows.
  • High attention to detail, including names, designations, dates, context, tone, grammar, formatting, and follow-up discipline.
  • Must have a strong bias for action and the ability to move things forward without repeated reminders.

What Good Looks Like
Success in this role means:
  • Founder outreach goes out on time, with the right tone and context.
  • Member communication feels personal, premium, and never generic.
  • Griffin event communication is sharp, timely, and well-structured.
  • Government and institutional communication feels mature, respectful, and credible.
  • The team has ready-to-use templates, message banks, and communication systems.
  • Important follow-ups do not get missed.
  • Griffin s voice becomes sharper, more consistent, and more distinctive over time.
  • Communication helps strengthen trust, increase founder participation, support retention, and elevate Griffin s overall brand.brand.
  • Who This Role Is Not For
  • This role may not be the right fit if:
  • You need very detailed instructions before starting any draft.
  • You write long when the situation requires sharpness.
  • You struggle to understand nuance, hierarchy, or relationship context.
  • You are comfortable with generic communication.
  • You wait for others to chase you before moving things forward.
  • You cannot handle multiple workstreams at once.
  • You do not enjoy operating close to founders, senior stakeholders, and high-expectation environments.

Reporting
The role will work closely with the Founder s Office and Griffin leadership team.

Role Summary
Griffin operates in rooms where trust, timing, language, and discretion matter deeply.

The Communication Lead will help shape how India s top founders experience Griffin - before an event, during a conversation, after a meeting, at the time of renewal, and in every important moment in between.

This role is for someone who wants to build the communication engine of a serious founder institution - not by shouting louder, but by writing sharper, thinking deeper, and moving faster.

More about the role


Job Summary

The Regional (Site IT / Hub) Lead is responsible for leading and coordinating user support services within a defined / assigned region. This role ensures that employees receive timely, professional, and effective IT support for workplace technology, including laptops, mobile devices, collaboration tools, business applications, and office IT services. The Team Lead acts as the first point of escalation for support issues, manages the day-to-day performance of the regional support team, and works closely with global teams of infrastructure and security. In addition, collaborates with business stakeholders to deliver a consistent and high-quality support experience. The Regional Site IT Lead is responsible for and will oversee local Field Service Support engineers, Digital Technical Engineers and Service desk agents in a specific DigITal Hub location, and oversee field support for all sites assigned in the region

The Regional Site IT Lead is focused on helping end users to make better use of IT solutions. This will lead to improved productivity as well as improved customer satisfaction.

Key Areas of Responsibility

1. Team Leadership

  • Lead, coach, and support a regional team of Technical Engineers, Site IT Leads and Service desk agents.
  • Coordinate daily support activities, workloads, priorities, and shift coverage across the region (s).
  • Provide guidance on complex incidents, service requests, escalations,
  • Support team development through mentoring, feedback, knowledge sharing, and performance input.
  • Promote a customer-focused, professional, and service-oriented team culture.

2. End user support delivery

  • Ensure high-quality support for end user devices, operating systems, productivity tools, collaboration platforms, printers, peripherals, Fixed and mobile telephony, and standard business applications.
  • Oversee incident and service request handling in line with agreed service levels.
  • Monitor ticket queues to ensure timely resolution, proper prioritization, and accurate documentation.
  • Act as an escalation point for unresolved or high-impact support issues.
  • Support onboarding, offboarding, device deployment, asset replacement, and office moves.
  • Ensure the regional IT Service desks executes issues and requests in line with expectations, and in accordance to the Global Service desk owner.
  • Daily management of activities with the team

3. Regional IT Operations

  • Coordinate local and regional IT support activities across offices, sites, or countries within the assigned region.
  • Ensure regional support processes operate with global IT standards, policies, and procedures.
  • Partner with global teams to support infrastructure, network, security, IAM and application-related activities.
  • Act as regional hub lead for other teams within the same region of hub
  • Assist with regional rollouts, technology refreshes, software deployments, and change initiatives.
  • Maintain awareness of regional business needs, local constraints, and service improvement opportunities.

4. Asset, Compliance security

  • Ensure accurate management of IT assets, including laptops, mobile devices, accessories, and peripherals.
  • Support hardware lifecycle activities, inventory controls, forecasting, disposals. and audit requirements in alignment with Global Hardware Asset Manager.
  • Ensure end user support activities follow company security policies and compliance standards.
  • Promote secure working practices, including device encryption, access control, patching, and data protection.
  • Escalate security incidents or policy breaches through the appropriate channels.

5. Service coordinator

  • Manage relationships with managed (security) service providers.
  • Acts as local host in global projects, roll-outs adaptive change requests.
  • Provide insight in impact that global initiatives have on local business.
  • Monitor all IT incidents requests escalated by users in the local domain.

  • Track support performance, recurring issues, service trends, and user feedback.

  • Team leadership and coaching.

  • Ownership, accountability, and attention to detail.

  • Proven experience in end user support, desktop support, service desk, or workplace technology support.

title: Sr Data Platform Engineer(Microsoft Fabric,MLOps)
